- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in next 5-7 days; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment swings sharply upward (e.g., >1.5) followed by a drop, model frequently underestimates the subsequent decline; add a 2-3% downward bias in the following 3-5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 3-5 days after a strong negative sentiment event; apply a 3-5% upward bias for the first 5 days post-negative sentiment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.2–1.0), model often underestimates true price; add 2-4% upward bias for next 5-7 days.
- Model tends to lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is rising, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast by 2–5% for days 1–7 if sentiment is >0.5.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates true price; apply 5–8% upward bias for next 7–10 days to account for sentiment reversal.
